The Ishir, called Chamacoco by outsiders, are an Indigenous people of the northern Paraguayan Chaco, along the upper Paraguay River. The Ybytoso are the river group, around Bahía Negra and Puerto Diana; another group, the Tomárãho, lived inland. Their language belongs to the small Zamucoan family, with that of the Ayoreo.

They hunted, fished and gathered in the dry forest and along the river. They are known for their rich ceremonies, with feather costumes and masked figures that stand for powerful spirit beings.

In the 1900s many Ishir worked in the tannin factories and ranches along the river. The Chaco War of 1932 to 1935 was fought across the Chaco around them. Today a few thousand live in Paraguay. Other Chaco peoples include the Enxet.
